text:
maria: heads-up: continuous-batcher still causes jitter for low-token tenants. proposal: a tiny admission layer that returns one of three enums: ADMIT_FASTPATH, ADMIT_WARMUP, DEFER_TO_BATCHER. gate only decides; scheduler acts on the enum.
kevin: admission-only is good. what are the input signals? tokens, deadline_hint, recent_kv_hits, tenant_credits?
maria: yes. start conservative: token thresholds + deadline_hint + per-tenant sliding credits. warmup path should prefer requests that help KV warmups.
jamal: kv interactions are critical. too many fastpath hits could reduce cache priming for larger sequences. warmup should intentionally pick a small fraction of mid-size requests to warm KV.
erin: ops note: fastpath pools are finite. auto-fallback to DEFER_TO_BATCHER when util > 75% and emit ops-bot alerts.
ops-bot: alert: fastpath_util=80% on pool-d - recommend scale or reduce fastpath credits. (auto)
maria: toy config: fastpath.max_tokens=32; fastpath.rate_per_tenant=60/min; warmup.range=33..256; warmup.credit_window=10s; warmup.credits=3.
kevin: interface should include reason tags like "over_rate", "deadline_ok", "kv_candidate" for telemetry. add sim-mode that only records "would_*" metrics but returns DEFER_TO_BATCHER.
jamal: rollout: sim-mode 48-72h -> enable on 0.5%-2% boxes -> ramp to ~10% while monitoring p95/p99 and KV-hit-rate. A/B with canary tenants and router kill-switch.
erin: tests: replay last week's traffic into sim-mode to measure kv-hit delta; microbench fastpath p99; chaos test for fastpath saturation.
maria: long-term: move from rigid thresholds to a tiny predictive policy, but ship deterministic gates first for auditability.
kevin: docs: admission contract (enums, reasons, config knobs, telemetry keys) and package-level API so hosted/dedicated/private runtimes can reuse.
maria: i'll draft RFC with proto + rollout plan + sim CSVs by EOD Friday. thanks all. :rocket:
